set.body:
WHY: WLTrace symmetrizes every edge with one key, so a directed labelled edge is indistinguishable from its reverse; for predicate-argument structure (ARG0 vs ARG1 fillers) role reversal is invisible. Related earlier bead: grakern-e8-directed (directed attributed graph support) — this bead supersedes/realizes it through the neighbourhood protocol.

SCOPE: WL refinement consumes Incidence.orientation: the neighbourhood multiset element becomes (edgeKey, orientation, neighbourColour); OA features and subtree features inherit it. Undirected inputs use Orientation.Undirected and must reproduce today's behaviour exactly.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (laws G1/G2 from storymodel4s ADR 0001)
G1 Direction: for a directed graph g and g' = g with one edge reversed (or two filler vertices swapped across two differently-keyed edges), features(g) != features(g') and k(g,g') < k(g,g) after round >= 1.
G2 Invariance: alpha-renaming vertex ids and any permutation of incidence/edge enumeration order leave features, gram and cross bit-identical.
Parity: undirected inputs produce bit-identical results to the pre-change implementation (fixture goldens).
Fingerprint: SemanticFingerprint changes when orientation participates (version bump of the WL codec), so cached artifacts from the undirected era are never silently reused for directed inputs.

PROPOSED TESTS
- DirectedWLSuite: hand oracles — path a->b->c vs a<-b->c; star with two out-edges vs one in one out; ARG0/ARG1 swap on a 3-vertex predicate graph; assert feature multisets differ at round 1 and kernel drops.
- ScalaCheck property: forAll(digraph, permutation of vertex ids, shuffle of edge order) features equal (G2).
- ScalaCheck property: forAll(digraph with >=1 edge whose reversal is not an automorphism) features differ (G1) — generate and skip automorphic cases explicitly.
- ParityUnchangedSuite reused (all fixtures Undirected).
- CodecVersionSuite: fingerprint(directed codec) != fingerprint(legacy) on the same undirected input.
